definitions.explanation: The process of absorbing sound waves to reduce echo and reverberation. Used in acoustics, architecture, and interior design.

examples.japanese: {吸音|きゅうおん}{材|ざい}を{壁|かべ}に{貼|は}る。
examples.english: To apply sound-absorbing material to the walls.

examples.japanese: この{部屋|へや}は{吸音|きゅうおん}{性能|せいのう}が{高|たか}い。
examples.english: This room has high sound absorption performance.

examples.japanese: {会議室|かいぎしつ}の{天井|てんじょう}に{吸音|きゅうおん}パネルを{取|と}り{付|つ}けて{反響|はんきょう}を{抑|おさ}えた。
examples.english: Sound-absorbing panels were installed on the meeting room ceiling to reduce echo.

notes: Composed of {吸|きゅう} (absorb, inhale) + {音|おん} (sound). Distinct from {遮音|しゃおん} (sound insulation, which blocks sound transmission) and {防音|ぼうおん} (soundproofing, the general term). {吸音|きゅうおん} specifically reduces echo and reverberation within a space. Common collocations: {吸音|きゅうおん}{材|ざい} (sound-absorbing material), {吸音|きゅうおん}パネル (acoustic panel), {吸音|きゅうおん}{率|りつ} (sound absorption coefficient), {吸音|きゅうおん}{効果|こうか} (sound absorption effect). Materials like felt, foam, and perforated boards are common {吸音|きゅうおん}{材|ざい}.
